@aeschynanthus has made a comment below linking to his investigation of the front page ranking Please upvote him and reward him for his good work!

I am including the linked information here for the sake of completeness and to satisfy people who need a more detailed look at how this works.

NB. I don't really know much C# and I hope I didn't make mathematical errors.

I dug a little around Voat's source code and found the code for front page.

There's a long query that ends .OrderByDescending(s => s.Rank). So it orders the posts by descending rank. The rank is calculated in Utils/Ranking.cs:

var newRank = (Math.Pow((score - 1), 0.8)) / (Math.Pow((submissionAge + 2), 1.8)) * penalty;

Written in a less programmer-y way that becomes newRank = (score - 1)^0.8/ ((submissionAge+2)^1.8)*penalty. It does this:

  • take the score of the post
  • subtract one from that
  • raise the result to power 0.8. Call the result x.
  • take the submission's age in hours
  • add two hours to the age
  • raise the result to power 1.8. Call this result y
  • calculate x/y
  • multiply the result of this division by "penalty", which is defined to be 1 in the source, it doesn't do anything. Hm, if the precedence in C# is the expected, this multiplication happens last and isn't taken into "y". But as I said, it doesn't do anything since the penalty is 1.

If the score happens to be zero or negative, the raising to power of 0.8 doesn't give an answer, so the code gives rank of zero instead.

I made an example calculation with 25 items. They don't need titles but I used alphabet :p

I'm taking a moment to say what happened in my recent (ongoing) Microsoft support experience.

I own a Nokia Lumia 1520. One day the headphones started failing. I sent it in for repair, and it was sent back to me stating that there was liquid damage. I know I never dropped it in water or had it rained on, etc. So, I was quite surprised. I looked at the only LDI available to me and it was still white. No corrosion on the exposed metal, either. I live in Arkansas, so I guess the humidity...

I called Microsoft support for help. They explained their process (of which I was fully aware having formerly worked in Verizon Tech Support). I asked them if they could send me a picture or link to somewhere that they captured an image or video with evidence that the phone had been exposed to liquid. They woman on the phone put me on hold for a few minutes and came back with an offer. Since they couldn't verify it that way, they offered to replace the phone with a refurbished 1520 as a one-time courtesy. They said that they were currently out of stock, but that they would replace it once stock was available.

That was two months ago. I was wondering if they had forgotten about me. They have sent an email once a month to let me know they haven't, but how am I supposed to know if that's automated. I got a call today that I missed from Microsoft. They hadn't forgotten about me!I called them back with my reference number. The lady on the phone said that they had a 1520 for me, but it wasn't exactly the same--it is green and only 16GB instead of 32. As part of the deal, since it's a different phone they offered to send a portable USB charger, as well.

I was very pleased with this offer and accepted.
Update: My phone came in today. I did not realize that green would be so bright. I can go jogging on a moonless night and still be seen. Might even be able to land a plane with this thing.

I'm an unemployed woman in my mid-twenties, and highly educated. I went to grad school in Europe, I've published academic papers, and I've always been pretty well liked. Then life kind of kicked me in the teeth (or maybe my stupidity did, I'm not sure). I decided academia was not for me (for varied and extensive reasons, which I'm happy to elaborate on), and I became convinced that I'd much prefer a job at a non-profit, or working for the government. As it turns out, it was much harder to break into those industries than I'd expected. I moved in with my parents, who now live on the other side of the country from where I grew up, in the same small Southern town where I went to undergrad. It's a far cry different from the European cities to which I got accustomed, with little to do and very little diversity. I took a low paying job at a restaurant as a temporary way to pay the bills. "Temporary" became a year and a half, when I was laid off because the restaurant closed.

I continue to apply for jobs, but my steam is diminishing. I live in a town I had never planned on returning to, and have friend with whom I have very little in common. I live with my parents for the first time since I was 15, and I am beginning to struggle to see a way out of this hole. I started playing MMOs as a means of human contact and stayed for the false sense of positive reinforcement it gave me. I'm a person I don't like, someone I never was before. I do exercise (I've always been a bit of a gym rat), but I can only be at the gym so many hours of the day, milking those sweet sweet endorphins.

I fully recognize that I am still much more fortunate than most and that only I can work my way out of this. I'd just like a kick in the ass. Maybe some accountability?
